lines.latex: \text{What is the physics of a bridge?}
lines.plain: What is the physics of a bridge?

actions.text: A suspension bridge hangs its deck from cables. The cables are pulled tight (tension) and rest on the towers, which are squeezed (compression) and pass the weight into the ground. Turn the model and tap a part to see its job.

parts.name: Deck
parts.explain: The road. It bends under the traffic between hangers and hands its weight to the hangers every few metres.

parts.name: Left tower
parts.explain: The main cables rest on its top, so the whole deck's weight pushes straight down through it into the ground: compression.

parts.name: Left anchorage
parts.explain: A huge block of concrete that holds the cable ends down. Its weight resists the cable's pull.

parts.name: Right tower
parts.explain: The main cables rest on its top, so the whole deck's weight pushes straight down through it into the ground: compression.

parts.name: Right anchorage
parts.explain: A huge block of concrete that holds the cable ends down. Its weight resists the cable's pull.

parts.name: Main cable (north)
parts.explain: Hangs between the towers and is pulled tight by everything hanging from it, so it is in tension all along.
